rosters.notes: 384 students. Both group columns state their value once for a run of students and merge the rest of the run, so the merged ranges are what defines a cohort, not the rows. The subgroup column writes 'a1' where the schema says 'A1'; the mapping is declared value by value rather than case-folded, because Turkish upper-casing turns 'i' into 'İ' and would invent a cohort out of an English list (ADR-130). The list states no anatomyGroup, which Grade 2 Turkish also requires, so a student always enters that one. Three numbers begin '97' rather than the faculty code '01' and are refused by StudentProfileValidator, so those students cannot save a profile today. Two numbers are stored numerically and have lost a leading zero. Student number 0101240080 is also on the Grade 3 Turkish list, which makes it ambiguous.

113 students. The Grade 2 English program is deliberately absent from the supported profile schema (ADR-084), so this list suggests nothing until that program opens; it is catalogued because the document exists and its shape is now known. The two dimensions are genuinely independent and the document proves it: the İ1/İ2 boundary falls on row 56 while the i1/i2/i3 boundaries fall on rows 34 and 78, so i2 spans both general groups. They must not be collapsed on the grounds that their labels differ mostly by typography (ADR-085). One number is stored numerically and has lost a leading zero. The faculty publishes given names and surnames already masked here.

331 students in two merged runs: rows 2-169 are the A curriculum group and rows 170-332 the B one. The list states the curriculum group only. Grade 3 Turkish also requires facultyPracticeGroup, and the faculty has not assigned those cohorts for 2026-2027 yet, so a student always enters that one. One number is stored numerically and has lost a leading zero, one begins '97' rather than the faculty code and is refused by StudentProfileValidator, and 0101240080 is also on the Grade 2 Turkish list. The used range runs to column Z although only A-D hold anything.

96 students. It states no curriculum group, because the Grade 3 English program has no A/B division of its own (ADR-098); it still confirms identity, and it now merges with the microbiology/pathology list below, which does state an English student's practice group. Its header is written 'OgrenciNo' without Turkish letters or a space, unlike the other three. No malformed numbers.

426 students in one file covering both programs — the Turkish (0101…) and English (0102…) Grade 3 students — split into four microbiology/pathology practice groups A1/A2/B1/B2 in four merged runs of column D (rows 2-107, 108-213, 214-319, 320-427). The group column has no header, so it is addressed by letter. This Turkish entry claims only the 0101 rows via studentNumberProgramPrefix; the English entry below claims the 0102 rows from the same file (ADR-145). It complements G3-TR-ROSTER, which states the curriculum group, so a Grade 3 Turkish student is on both lists and the lookup merges them. One number begins '97' rather than the faculty code and is not this program's, so it is skipped by both program entries. Two numbers are stored numerically and have lost a leading zero, restored on read.

The English half of the shared microbiology/pathology group list (ADR-145): the same file as the Turkish entry above, claiming only the 0102 rows. It is what makes Grade 3 English onboardable — the only list of the program that states a cohort — and it merges with G3-EN-ROSTER, which confirms identity but states no group. 96 English students across the same four A1/A2/B1/B2 groups.
